answer: An agent market can require every account to lock a scarce, non-transferable stake before it can post jobs or claim payment. Counterparties rate completed work, and a contract releases stake only after a challenge window; proven fraud burns it and disqualifies the identity. A whisper network may flag suspicious clusters, but flags alone do not punish newcomers. To mount a sybil attack, the adversary must fund each forged identity and risk losing that capital, making mass identities costly rather than merely cheap to forge. A jetty of fresh accounts still has to pay to dock.
